mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 QoQ decline does not correlate with subsequent economic contraction indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO MoM increase does not correlate with subsequent economic expansion indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy and inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) and falling nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of rising UNRATE and falling PAYEMS does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent consumer demand indicators.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a decrease in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter signals a contractionary effect, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 QoQ decline does not correlate with subsequent economic contraction indicators during a tightening cycle.
